mainTopic: Removing disgusting things on שבת, and the משנה listing שבות, רשות, and מצוה acts forbidden on יום טוב as on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about covering a beehive on שבת. The גמרא re-reads its condition as 'provided he does not make it a trap,' and teaches that even bees count for צידה. רב אשי gives another reading: the ברייתא means ניסן and תשרי, when there is honey in the hive. Next comes the משנה's rule that you may put a כלי under a leak on שבת and empty it as often as needed. This leads to the story of אביי's leaking millhouse, where רבה used the rule of גרף של רעי. Then שמואל's rule about removing waste containers, and רב אשי's mouse, which shows that disgusting things may be removed even without a vessel. A new משנה teaches that acts forbidden on שבת as שבות, רשות, or מצוה are also forbidden on יום טוב, and that the only difference between the two days is אוכל נפש. The גמרא then explains the reason for each שבות and begins asking why judging and betrothal are called only 'optional.' The answer about betrothal continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Re-reading the condition: do not make it a trap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes how we read the ברייתא's condition. It is not about what the person intends. It is about not covering the hive in a way that turns it into a trap.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: provided he does not make it into a trap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes a difficulty from the earlier discussion by reading the ברייתא's condition a new way. You may spread mats over the hive, as long as you do not turn the hive into a trap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier wording, 'as long as he does not intend to trap,' caused a problem. So the גמרא says to read it as a practical rule: do not seal the hive completely. If you leave openings, the bees are not being trapped.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (a signal that the גמרא is re-reading a text)

phrases.english: Rather, say:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to re-read the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Provided that he does not make it a trap.
phrases.notes: In other words, he must not cover every opening of the hive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty raised on the previous amud about the ברייתא's original wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The condition was about the person's intent to trap.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition is about the physical act: do not close up the hive so that it becomes a trap.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to tell us not to trap the bees. Trapping is a well-known מלאכה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading by saying it is too obvious to need saying. This sets up the next step, which explains what we actually learn from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צידה (trapping) is one of the forbidden מלאכות of שבת. So a ruling that you may not make the hive into a trap seems to add nothing new. A ברייתא is not supposed to teach something everyone already knows.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a teaching adds nothing new)

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: Why would the ברייתא need to say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new reading from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's condition, 'provided he does not make it a trap.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trapping on שבת is clearly forbidden, so stating it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The new point: even bees count for trapping
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא needed to say it. Otherwise we might think that only animals people usually hunt are forbidden to trap, and that bees are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: a type of animal that people usually trap is forbidden to trap, but a type that people do not usually trap is allowed. So the ברייתא teaches us that it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge. It shows there was a real mistake someone could make, and the ברייתא prevents it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the איסור of צידה only applies to animals that are normally hunted, and bees are not. The ברייתא teaches that even an animal not normally hunted, like a bee, may not be trapped on שבת. That is the new information.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
A type of animal that is usually trapped

steps.whatToRemember: On this reading, the ברייתא allows covering the hive but forbids sealing it like a trap. Even creatures that are not usually hunted, like bees, count for צידה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
phrases.notes: Here comes the mistake the ברייתא wants to prevent.

phrases.english: A type that is usually trapped is forbidden,
but a type that is not usually trapped is permitted,
phrases.notes: Bees would fall into this group.

phrases.english: So it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: blocking a possible mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Animals that are not usually hunted, like bees, may be trapped on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even animals that are not usually hunted may not be trapped on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that the מלאכה of צידה is not limited to animals people usually hunt.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא means ניסן and תשרי, when there is honey
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer. The ברייתא never said 'summer' and 'rainy season.' It said 'in the sun because of the sun, and in the rain because of the rain.' That describes ניסן and תשרי, when there is honey in the hive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Does the ברייתא say 'in the summer days and in the rainy days'? It says 'in the sun because of the sun, and in the rain because of the rain.' This means the days of ניסן and the days of תשרי, when there is sun, there is rain, and there is honey.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes a different route to solve the earlier problem. He reads the ברייתא as talking about seasons when the hive has honey in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier difficulty assumed the ברייתא meant full summer and full winter, when the hive has no honey. רב אשי points out that the wording is about sun and rain, not seasons. Both happen in ניסן and תשרי, when there is honey, so covering the hive can be for the honey, just as first suggested.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually teach...? (questioning a reading of the text)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not rejecting the case itself. He is just pointing out that 'sun' and 'rain' do not have to mean the full summer and winter seasons.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: the ברייתא is talking about ניסן and תשרי. There is honey in the hive then, so covering it is to protect the honey.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
phrases.notes: This is a different approach from steps 1 through 3.

phrases.aramaic: מִי קָתָנֵי בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וּבִימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים?
phrases.english: Does it teach 'in the summer days and in the rainy days'?
phrases.notes: No, it does not.

phrases.english: 'In the sun because of the sun'
and 'in the rain because of the rain' is what it teaches,
meaning the days of Nisan and the days of Tishrei,
phrases.notes: Spring and autumn.

phrases.english: when there is sun, and there is rain,
and there is honey.
phrases.notes: So the covering can be for the honey.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מִי קָתָנֵי בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וּבִימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different solution to the problem that step 1 was solving.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the text's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about summer and winter, when there is no honey.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about ניסן and תשרי, when there is honey, so the covering is for the honey.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a כלי under a leak on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. On שבת, you may put a container under a leak.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may place a vessel under a leak on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. The משנה allows catching leaking water in a כלי on שבת, so the house does not get damaged. The next step will add a detail to this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A leak (water dripping from the roof)

phrases.english: And one may place a vessel under a leak on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may put a כלי under a leak on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא: empty the full כלי and put it back, again and again
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that if the כלי fills up, you may pour it out and put it back under the leak, as many times as needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if the vessel became full, he pours it out and does it again, and he does not need to hold back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a detail to the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought you may only put the כלי down once. The ברייתא says you may keep emptying it and putting it back. There is no limit on how many times.

keyTerms.meaning: And he does not hold back

phrases.english: It was taught: If the vessel became full,
he pours it out and repeats, and he does not refrain.
phrases.notes: He may do this as many times as needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full כלי may be emptied and put back under the leak as many times as needed.

steps.title: אביי's millhouse is leaking
steps.stepSummary: On שבת, אביי's millhouse sprang a leak. He went to רבה to ask what to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי's millhouse was leaking. He came before רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story. אביי has a real-life problem on שבת and brings it to his teacher רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leaking water could ruin the millstones. Simply emptying containers would not be enough. The water was dirty and not fit to use, so it was מוקצה and could not just be carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: He came before him (to ask a question)

phrases.english: Abaye's millhouse was leaking.
phrases.notes: This happened on שבת.

phrases.english: He came before Rabba,
phrases.notes: To ask what to do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life case connected to the topic of leaks on שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can he protect the millhouse from the dirty, מוקצה leaking water on שבת?

steps.title: רבה: bring your bed in, so the water becomes like a גרף של רעי
steps.stepSummary: רבה tells אביי to bring his bed into the millhouse. Then the dirty water counts as a גרף של רעי, which may be removed because it is disgusting.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go bring your bed in there, so that it will be like a chamber pot of excrement, and then take it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי with a clever solution. Once someone sleeps in that room, the dirty water becomes something disgusting that you are allowed to remove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גרף של רעי is מוקצה, but the חכמים allowed removing it from where people are because it is disgusting. By making the millhouse a place where he lives, אביי turns the dirty water into that kind of disgusting thing. Then he may carry it out.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber pot of excrement (may be removed on שבת because it is disgusting)

steps.whatToRemember: Something disgusting that is in a place where people live may be removed on שבת even though it is מוקצה. You can even bring yourself into that situation on purpose, like moving your bed in.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying the water stops being מוקצה. It stays מוקצה. The permission to remove it comes from the special rule for גרף של רעי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that you may set up a situation that brings the leniency of גרף של רעי into play, so you can protect your property on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל עַיְּילֵיהּ לְפוּרְיָךְ לְהָתָם,
phrases.english: He said to him: Go, bring your bed in there,
phrases.notes: Into the millhouse.

phrases.english: so that it will be like a chamber pot of excrement,
phrases.notes: Something disgusting that may be removed.

phrases.english: and then take it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל עַיְּילֵיהּ לְפוּרְיָךְ לְהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה's answer to אביי's question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bring your bed into the millhouse, so the water is treated like a גרף של רעי and may be removed.

steps.title: אביי questions רבה's advice
steps.stepSummary: אביי sits and wonders: is a person allowed to deliberately create a גרף של רעי situation in the first place?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי sat and found it difficult: Do we make a container of excrement on purpose, from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי has a problem with the advice רבה just gave him. Bringing a bed into the millhouse would deliberately turn the dirty water into something disgusting, just so it could be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission to remove a גרף של רעי is meant for a disgusting situation that already exists. אביי questions whether you may set up such a situation yourself, on purpose, as a way around the שבת rules. He is challenging רבה's ruling from Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, deliberately, ahead of time

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not asking whether one may remove a גרף של רעי. That is already allowed. He is asking whether one may deliberately create the disgusting situation in order to rely on that permission.

phrases.english: Abaye sat, and it was difficult for him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי עוֹשִׂין גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי לְכַתְּחִלָּה?
phrases.english: Do we make a container of excrement deliberately, from the start?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer from Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's advice to bring a bed into the millhouse so the water becomes a גרף של רעי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The removal permission covers disgusting situations that already exist. It should not allow a person to create such a situation on purpose.

steps.title: The millhouse collapses and אביי blames himself
steps.stepSummary: While אביי was still thinking it over, his millhouse collapsed. He said this happened because he had questioned his teacher's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, אביי's millhouse collapsed. He said: This came upon me because I went against the word of my master.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with אביי's millhouse falling down while he was still deliberating. He sees the collapse as a punishment for not following רבה right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story ends with a lesson about respecting your teacher, not with a legal answer to אביי's question. By delaying, אביי lost the very building he was trying to save. רבה's advice stands as the practical guidance in the story.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile, in the middle of this
Let it come upon me; I deserve this
That I went against the word of my master

steps.whatToRemember: The story ends with אביי admitting he should have followed רבה. The idea of turning water into a גרף של רעי by bringing in a bed is left as accepted advice.

phrases.english: Meanwhile, Abaye's millhouse collapsed.
He said: I had this coming to me for going against the word of my master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in Step 7, closing off אביי's challenge from Step 9
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי accepts that he should have followed רבה's advice without delay.

steps.title: שמואל on removing waste containers
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that containers of excrement and of urine may be taken out to the garbage heap on שבת. When bringing one back, he must first put water in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A container of excrement and a container of urine may be taken out to the garbage heap. When he brings it back, he puts water in it and then brings it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related rule from שמואל about removing disgusting containers on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the container out is allowed because it is disgusting, and that permission is the גרף של רעי rule. Once the container is empty, that reason is gone, and the dirty container on its own is מוקצה. Putting water in it gives it a use, so it may be carried back.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the permission to move something because it is disgusting covers only what is needed. It does not cover carrying the empty container back.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי וְעָבִיט שֶׁל מֵימֵי רַגְלַיִם —
phrases.english: A container of excrement and a pot of urine,
it is permitted to take them out to the garbage heap.
And when he brings it back,
he puts water in it and brings it back.
phrases.notes: The water gives the empty, smelly container a use, so it is no longer forbidden to carry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the גרף של רעי rule mentioned in Step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waste containers may be taken out to the garbage heap on שבת. They may be brought back only after water is put in them.

steps.title: An inference: only removal inside a vessel
steps.stepSummary: Some people learned from שמואל's wording that disgusting matter may be removed only together with its vessel, and not by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this: A גרף של רעי together with its vessel, yes. By itself, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a conclusion that some people drew from שמואל's words. It is setting up the next step, which will show that this conclusion is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל spoke about containers, so some people concluded that the permission depends on there being a vessel. On that reading, you could not pick up the disgusting thing directly.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it; they assumed
Together with (by means of) the vessel

phrases.english: They understood from it:

phrases.aramaic: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי, אַגַּב מָנָא — אִין,
phrases.english: A container of excrement, together with the vessel, yes;
by itself, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a limiting inference from שמואל's ruling in Step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed reading: disgusting matter may be removed only inside its vessel.

steps.title: רב אשי's mouse shows direct removal is allowed
steps.stepSummary: A dead mouse was found in רב אשי's spice storeroom. He told them to pick it up by its tail and take it out, which shows that disgusting things may be removed directly, even without a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A mouse was found in רב אשי's spice storeroom. רב אשי told them: Grab it by its tail and take it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that disproves the inference from Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead mouse is מוקצה and disgusting, and here it was handled directly, with no vessel at all. So the permission to remove disgusting things does not depend on a vessel. The limited reading of שמואל is rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: A disgusting item may be removed on שבת even by itself, picked up directly. The permission is not limited to taking it out inside a vessel.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
That a certain mouse was found
in Rav Ashi's spice storeroom.
Rav Ashi said to them:
Grab it by its tail and take it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference from Step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that disgusting matter may be removed only inside a vessel
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אשי allowed a dead mouse to be removed directly, by hand, with no vessel.

steps.title: New משנה: שבת restrictions apply on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה states that anything forbidden on שבת because of שְׁבוּת, רְשׁוּת, or מִצְוָה is also forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Anything that is forbidden on שבת because of a שְׁבוּת, a רְשׁוּת, or a מִצְוָה is also forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out a general rule linking rabbinic שבת restrictions to יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three groups are rabbinic restrictions, not forbidden מלאכה from the תורה. The משנה teaches that יום טוב is just as strict as שבת for them. The list of examples follows in the next part of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic restriction for the sake of resting
An optional act (that still has some aspect of a מצוה)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean that a רְשׁוּת or a מִצְוָה is forbidden in general. It means certain acts with these qualities, which are still restricted on שבת, stay restricted on יום טוב too.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת,
phrases.english: MISHNA: Anything for which one is liable because of a rabbinic rest decree,
because of an optional act, or because of a מצוה, on Shabbat,
one is liable for it on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rabbinic שבת restrictions in the categories of שְׁבוּת, רְשׁוּת, and מִצְוָה apply equally on יום טוב.

steps.title: The list of acts forbidden as rabbinic restrictions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the acts forbidden because of שבות: climbing a tree, riding an animal, swimming, clapping, slapping the thigh, and dancing.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are forbidden because of שבות: One may not climb a tree, nor ride on an animal, nor swim in the water, nor clap hands, nor slap the thigh, nor dance.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now explains the first category from step 14 by listing everyday acts that חכמים forbade as שבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these acts is a real מלאכה from the תורה. חכמים forbade them as a protective fence. Climbing a tree could lead to tearing off a branch, and riding could lead to cutting a stick to drive the animal. Swimming could lead to making a floating device, and clapping or dancing could lead to fixing a musical instrument.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic restriction on שבת or יום טוב, made to keep a person away from real מלאכה
Clapping one hand against the other
Slapping the hand on the thigh

steps.confusionAlert: These acts are not forbidden because they are hard work in themselves. They are rabbinic fences (גזירות) that keep a person from coming to do a real מלאכה.

phrases.english: And these are the ones forbidden because of shevut (rabbinic rest):
One may not climb a tree,
phrases.notes: Out of concern he will tear off a branch.

phrases.english: nor ride on an animal,
phrases.notes: Out of concern he will cut a stick to drive it.

phrases.english: nor swim on the surface of the water,
phrases.notes: Out of concern he will make a float.

phrases.english: nor clap the hands, nor slap the thigh,
nor dance.
phrases.notes: Out of concern he will repair a musical instrument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first category (שבות) named in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Climbing trees, riding animals, swimming, clapping, thigh-slapping, and dancing are forbidden as שבות.

steps.title: The list of optional religious acts that are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists acts forbidden even though they are optional religious acts (רשות): judging, betrothing, חליצה, and יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are forbidden even though they are optional acts: One may not judge, nor betroth a woman, nor perform חליצה, nor perform יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the second category: acts with some מצוה value that are still forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These acts have a religious side, but they are not strict obligations at that moment, so they are called רשות. The concern is that they are like a court proceeding or a business deal, and they might lead to writing. So even their מצוה side does not permit them.

keyTerms.meaning: An optional act that has some מצוה value but is not a full obligation
Performing חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Here מִשּׁוּם רְשׁוּת does NOT mean 'permitted.' It means these acts are only optional מצוה acts, and they are still forbidden.

phrases.english: And these are forbidden despite being optional (religious) acts:
One may not judge, nor betroth a woman,
nor perform chalitza, nor perform levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the שבות list to the second category, רשות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Judging, קידושין, חליצה, and יבום are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.

steps.title: The list of full מצוה acts that are still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists acts forbidden even though they are real מצוות: consecrating, making a valuation vow, declaring חרם, and separating תרומה and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are forbidden even though they are מצוה acts: One may not consecrate property, nor make a valuation vow, nor declare property חרם, nor separate תרומה and מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third list. Even acts that are full מצוות are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list goes a step further than רשות: even a full מצוה does not override these rabbinic restrictions. Consecrating or declaring property is like transferring ownership, which looks like a business deal. Separating תרומה and מעשר looks like fixing the produce (מתקן).

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrating property to the בית המקדש (הקדש)
Making a valuation vow (ערכין), pledging a person's set value to the Temple
Declaring property חרם, dedicated to כהנים or the Temple
The portions of produce separated for the כהן and the לוי

steps.confusionAlert: Here מַחֲרִימִין means dedicating property (חרמים), not excommunicating a person.

phrases.english: And these are forbidden despite being מצוה acts:
One may not consecrate, nor make a valuation vow,
nor dedicate property as cherem,
nor separate teruma and tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three categories named in step 14 by listing the מצוה category.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדש, ערכין, חרמים, and separating תרומה ומעשר are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.

steps.title: If forbidden on יום טוב, surely forbidden on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says all these acts were stated about יום טוב, so they are surely forbidden on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: All these were stated about יום טוב; all the more so they are forbidden on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses a קל וחומר to stretch all three lists from יום טוב to שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום טוב is the more lenient day, since some מלאכה is allowed then. If these acts are forbidden even on the lenient day, they must surely be forbidden on the stricter day, שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from the lighter case to the stricter case

phrases.english: All these they stated regarding a Festival;
all the more so on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies all three lists to שבת through a קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whatever is forbidden on יום טוב as שבות, רשות, or מצוה is surely forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: The only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the general rule: יום טוב and שבת are the same except that food preparation is allowed on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no difference between יום טוב and שבת except for food preparation alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a general rule that compares יום טוב and שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule sums up the whole topic. The מלאכה permitted on יום טוב is limited to אוכל נפש, meaning work needed to prepare food. In every other area, יום טוב follows the same rules as שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Work needed to prepare food, which is permitted on יום טוב
'There is no difference between', the opening formula of a comparison rule

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three categories that are forbidden on both יום טוב and שבת: שבות, רשות, and מצוה. The only thing יום טוב permits beyond שבת is אוכל נפש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis for the laws of יום טוב: any מלאכה that is not for אוכל נפש stays forbidden, just as on שבת.

phrases.english: There is no difference between a Festival and Shabbat
except for food preparation alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין יוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת אֶלָּא אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ בִּלְבָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the קל וחומר into a general comparison rule between יום טוב and שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יום טוב and שבת differ only in that אוכל נפש is permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: Why one may not climb a tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens and explains that climbing a tree is forbidden as a גזירה, so that one will not pull off branches or fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: One may not climb a tree. This is a protective decree, so that he will not detach something from the tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and starts explaining the reasons for the משנה's list. Climbing a tree is forbidden so that the person will not end up pulling off leaves, branches, or fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Climbing a tree is not itself a מלאכה. But a person up in a tree can easily snap something off, and detaching a growing thing is the תורה-level מלאכה of reaping (קוצר). So the חכמים forbade climbing as a fence around that.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that explains the משנה
A protective rabbinic decree made to keep a person away from a real prohibition
He will detach (pull something off a growing plant)

steps.confusionAlert: Climbing itself is not a prohibition from the תורה. It is forbidden only because of what it might lead to.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
One may not climb a tree —
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: a decree, lest he detach (from the tree).
phrases.notes: Detaching is the מלאכה of reaping

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's explanation of the משנה's list of שבות acts from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Climbing a tree is forbidden lest one detach part of it.

steps.title: A first reason for not riding an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that riding an animal is forbidden so that one will not ride past the תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not ride on an animal. This is a decree, lest he go out beyond the תחום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first reason for the ban on riding an animal: a rider might travel past the תחום without noticing. This reason is about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On an animal a person moves quickly and far, so he could easily pass the 2,000-אמה limit (תחום). This step is a proposal, and the next step attacks it.

keyTerms.meaning: The boundary beyond which one may not walk on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: And one may not ride on an animal —
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: a decree, lest he go out beyond the boundary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down the משנה's list with the next item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed: riding is forbidden lest one leave the תחום.

steps.title: Would that prove תחומין are from the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if riding were forbidden to protect the תחום, it would prove that תחומין are a law from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that תחומין are from the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason just given. If the חכמים made a protective fence around תחומין, that suggests תחומין are a law from the תורה, which is a disputed point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים normally make a protective גזירה only around a prohibition from the תורה, not around something that is itself rabbinic. So protecting the תחום with a riding ban would imply that תחומין are from the תורה. Since that question is disputed, the גמרא does not want this משנה to settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (here used as a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real conclusion that תחומין are from the תורה. It is a challenge showing that the reason leads to an unwanted result, so the reason gets replaced.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic rule: a reason for a גזירה must fit with what we know about the status of the law it protects.

phrases.english: Learn from this
that boundaries are from the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason proposed in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that riding is forbidden lest one leave the תחום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזירה is made to protect a law from the תורה. So guarding the תחום would imply תחומין are from the תורה, which is a disputed matter that this משנה should not decide.

steps.title: The real reason: cutting a branch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא replaces the reason: riding is forbidden lest the rider cut a branch to use as a whip.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: it is a decree, lest he cut off a branch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the תחום reason and gives a new one. A rider might cut a stick from a tree to urge the animal on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a branch is reaping (קוצר), which is clearly a תורה-level מלאכה. That makes the riding ban a normal fence around a law from the תורה, and it says nothing about whether תחומין are from the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A branch or twig (used as a riding stick)

steps.whatToRemember: Riding an animal on שבת or יום טוב is forbidden lest one cut a branch to drive the animal. It is not because of the תחום.

phrases.english: Rather:
a decree, lest he cut a branch.
phrases.notes: To use as a whip for the animal

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 22 by giving a different reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Riding is forbidden lest one leave the תחום, which would imply תחומין are from the תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Riding is forbidden lest one cut a branch, which is a תורה-level מלאכה of reaping, so nothing is proven about תחומין.

steps.title: Why one may not swim
steps.stepSummary: Swimming is forbidden lest one make a floating barrel used by swimmers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not swim on the water. This is a decree, lest he make a swimmers' barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next item on the list. Swimming is forbidden so that one will not build a float to help him swim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beginners used a barrel or similar device to stay afloat. Making such an item is like making a utensil (תיקון כלי), which is a real מלאכה, so the חכמים banned swimming as a fence.

phrases.english: And one may not swim on the surface of the water —
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: a decree, lest he make
a swimmers' barrel.
phrases.notes: A flotation device

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יַעֲשֶׂה חָבִית שֶׁל שַׁיָּיטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the riding discussion ends, returns to explaining the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swimming is forbidden lest one make a swimmers' barrel.

steps.title: Why one may not clap or dance
steps.stepSummary: Clapping, slapping the thigh, and dancing are forbidden lest one fix a musical instrument.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not clap, slap the thigh, or dance. This is a decree, lest he fix a musical instrument.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list. Clapping, slapping the thigh, and dancing all share one reason: a person caught up in music might repair or make an instrument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These acts go with music. Someone who is clapping or dancing may want to adjust an instrument to play along, and fixing a כלי is a תורה-level מלאכה. So all three are banned together under one גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Slap the hand on the thigh

steps.whatToRemember: Every item on the שבות list is a protective גזירה tied to a real מלאכה: climbing (detaching), riding (cutting a branch), swimming (making a float), and clapping or dancing (fixing an instrument).

phrases.english: And one may not clap
nor slap the thigh, nor dance —
a decree, lest he fix musical instruments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the משנה's list of שבות acts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clapping, thigh-slapping, and dancing are forbidden lest one fix a musical instrument.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: judging is listed as optional
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next category of the משנה, acts that are forbidden 'because of רשות'. The first item is: one may not judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the things forbidden that are in the category of 'optional': one may not judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of 'optional' acts, starting with judging a court case. It is setting up a question about why judging is called optional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has three groups: שבות (plain rabbinic decrees), רשות (optional acts), and מצוה‎ (מצוה acts). Judging is placed in the רשות group. That placement suggests judging is not a full מצוה, and this is exactly what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: And these are; the opening of a list in the משנה
Because of / in the category of
Optional; an act that is allowed but not required

steps.confusionAlert: 'Optional' does not mean judging is allowed on שבת. Everything in this list is forbidden. 'Optional' only describes what kind of act it is on a normal weekday.

phrases.english: And these are [forbidden] in the category of optional acts:
One may not judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the שבות group (riding, swimming, clapping) to the next group in the משנה, the רשות acts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Judging on שבת is forbidden, and the משנה classifies it as an 'optional' act.

steps.title: But judging is a real מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: judging a case is a true מצוה, so why does the משנה call it optional?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is doing a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's label. Judging fairly is a real מצוה, so calling it 'optional' seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on the category, not on the rule. Nobody doubts that judging is forbidden on שבת. The question is only why the משנה files it under רשות instead of מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely; a word that opens a challenge
A commandment / a required good deed

phrases.english: But he is performing a מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the label 'optional' that step 26 gave to judging.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's placement of judging in the רשות category
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Judging is a full מצוה, so it should not be described as merely optional.

steps.title: Answer: someone better qualified is available
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a case where another judge, better than this one, is available. So for this person, judging is only optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where there is someone more qualified than him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is describing a specific case: a better judge is available. In that case it is not a real obligation for this person to judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Judging is still a מצוה in general. But when a more qualified person can take the case, this person's judging becomes a choice rather than a duty. The answer narrows the case and leaves the general category of judging as a מצוה untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for…; introduces a narrow case
Who is better / more qualified than him

steps.whatToRemember: Judging is called 'optional' only when a better judge is available. Then this particular person is not obligated to judge.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary [only for a case]
where there is someone more qualified than he.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Judging is always a full מצוה, so it cannot be called optional.
steps.terutzMaskana: When a more qualified judge is available, this person's judging is only optional.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: one may not betroth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item on the 'optional' list: one may not betroth a woman on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not betroth [a woman].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item from the משנה's 'optional' list, betrothing a woman (קידושין). It is setting up the same kind of question it just asked about judging.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Betrothal is a legal act, a bit like a business transaction, so the חכמים forbade it on שבת. The משנה again files it under רשות, which seems to say that getting married is not a full מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal; the first stage of Jewish marriage

phrases.english: Nor may one betroth [a woman].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the same list of רשות acts that began in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothing a woman on שבת is forbidden, and the משנה classifies it as optional.

steps.title: But marrying is a real מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats its challenge: marrying lets a person fulfill פריה ורביה, so it should be a real מצוה, not optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is doing a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the exact same challenge as before. Getting married is a real מצוה, so why does the משנה call it optional?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marriage makes it possible to fulfill פריה ורביה (having children), so betrothal looks like a full מצוה. Once again, the challenge targets the category label, not the prohibition itself.

phrases.english: But he is performing a מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same challenge as step 27, now aimed at betrothal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's placement of betrothal in the רשות category
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marriage enables פריה ורביה, so it is a full מצוה and should not be called optional.

steps.title: The answer begins: a specific case is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with 'לא צריכא'. As with judging, it will narrow the case. The rest of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed [for a specific case]…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer, using the same pattern as with judging. This passage ends in the middle of the answer, so the actual case appears on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening 'לא צריכא' tells us the answer will be a narrow case in which marrying is not a full obligation for this person. The continuation explains that he already has a wife and children, so he has already fulfilled פריה ורביה.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife and children; the case the answer will describe on the next amud

steps.confusionAlert: This step stops in mid-sentence. Do not treat 'לא צריכא' as the full answer. The specific case comes right on the next amud.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary [only for a case]…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 30, using the same pattern as step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (לא צריכא); continues on the next amud
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Betrothal is always a full מצוה because of פריה ורביה.
steps.terutzMaskana: (Continues on the next amud) In the specific case described, betrothal is only optional.
